sent:
Lena—

Your ethos is clear; the path to “this is the gift” is hidden. Here’s what to change for Q4, in the order we’d do it:

1) Homepage hero: make gifting the job. Example: “Handmade Brighton gifts under £100” → single CTA to a curated page.
2) Three gifting pages: For Her • Under £100 • Personalised. First screen: (a) one‑line promise, (b) 3 top picks with star ratings and price, (c) delivery/returns strip.
3) Nav and cards: add Gifts to top nav (Oct–Dec); add “Most Gifted”/“Under £100” badges on product tiles.
4) PDP first screen: add bullets above the fold—Recycled sterling silver; Handmade in Brighton; 4.8/5 from 180+ reviews; Free UK shipping over £75; Gift box/returns if offered. Keep Add to Cart visible on mobile.
5) Cart reassurance: repeat shipping threshold, delivery cut‑offs (when final), and returns in‑cart. Add “You’re £X from free shipping” message; surface payment marks. Consider showing the welcome 10% code in‑cart for new visitors.
6) Ads and landing pages: run 3 concepts × 3 variants—(a) hand‑worn close‑ups in sunlight, (b) gift unboxing, (c) maker‑at‑bench. Send each to its matching gifting page; retire any asset after three weeks of falling CTR.

Measure simply: tag links to each gifting page, route ~50% of paid traffic there for a clean read, and compare conversion rate and cost per first order against your current paths.

If you want, I can turn this into a simple wireframe for the hero and one gifting page.

Fieldwork Studio
